title: regional-failover-playbook-graceful-eviction-and-capacity-aware-probes
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create an operational playbook and implementation tasks for multi-region failover that emphasizes graceful eviction of in-flight work and capacity-aware readiness probes for warm standbys. The goal is to ensure customer traffic can be failed over to alternative regions or model variants with minimal latency spikes and no data loss, while avoiding cascading capacity overloads in target regions. This ticket covers probe design, eviction/drain semantics, progressive traffic shifts, model-variant compatibility checks, and observability hooks for post-failover diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Implement readiness probes that account for GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache warmness and surface a single boolean 'serving_ready' for routing decisions.
Failover orchestration can shift traffic using progressive percentages (0->25->50->100) with configurable hold times and automatic rollback on error spikes.
Graceful eviction drains existing requests with a configurable soft-deadline and does not accept new long-running requests after eviction start.
Fallback model variant compatibility checks validate tokenizer, sequence length, and quantization support before router swaps.
End-to-end integration test (simulated incident) demonstrates <20% P95 latency increase and no request loss for 95% of requests during failover to a warm standby region.
Dashboards and runbook entries exist for operators to inspect probe signals, failover timeline, and model-quality deltas post-failover.
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe logic (utilization thresholds, queue aging, cache-hit fraction).
End-to-end sim that injects 30% region outage and measures traffic migration metrics and latency percentiles.
Chaos test: induce spike in target region to verify circuit-breaker prevents overload and triggers rollback.
Quality regression test comparing outputs from primary model -> fallback model variant across representative prompt set.
implementation_notes: Probe composition: combine fast liveness (process + GPU driver) with slow readiness signals (GPU util, queue depth, cached KV hit rate) and expose a rolling 30s windowed score.
Use jittered probe schedules to avoid synchronized probe storms across many nodes (randomize by up to 200ms).

Capacity-aware routing: route prefers region with available 'serve_capacity' score (derived from free GPU VRAM, token/sec headroom, and queue depth) over absolute network latency once customer_impact is high.

Eviction semantics: mark instance 'evicting' -> stop accepting new long-running requests -> allow short responses to finish within soft_deadline (default 6s) -> hard_kill after hard_deadline (default 20s) if still alive.
Progressive traffic shift: controller steps percentages and monitors 'error_rate', 'p95_latency', and 'model_quality_score' before proceeding to next step.
Fallback model selection: prefer same-architecture quantized variant; if not compatible, validate at routing time with a lightweight smoke-run of representative prompt set under isolation.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18 - Ticket created after postmortem for region outage on 2025-02-15. Initial scope agreed with SRE and runtime teams.
2025-02-20 - Design review with SRE, runtime, and PM. Decided to implement consolidated 'serving_ready' boolean that aggregates signals; agreed on progressive shift behavior and eviction windows.
2025-02-24 - Prototype probe implemented (runtime/probes) exposing GPU util + queue depth. Initial tests show noisy signal for KV cache warmness — will use cache-hit-rate smoothing.
2025-02-26 - Draft runbook added to Confluence with operator play steps and rollback criteria. Feedback from Support requested clearer dashboard GLIs.
2025-03-03 - Integration tests added to CI: simulated region outage run. Found a race where progressive shift proceeded despite slow cache warmup; added gating on 'cache_warmth >= 0.6' metric.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive failover may overload target region -> Mitigation: capacity-aware gating and circuit-breaker with exponential backoff.
Risk: Fallback model variant reduces output quality -> Mitigation: run smoke-quality check and surface model_quality_score to routing controller; auto-rollback threshold configurable.
Risk: Probe noise causes flapping -> Mitigation: use rolling-window smoothing and require N consecutive failing windows before marking 'not ready'.
Risk: Long-lived requests hinder eviction -> Mitigation: introduce application-level soft deadlines and route-level enforcement for long requests.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge feature flags behind 'multi_region_failover_v2' and 'capacity_aware_probes'.
Step 1: Deploy probes-only to staging and collect signals for 48h.
Step 2: Enable progressive shift controller in staging and run chaos test (simulated AZ + region outage).
Step 3: Canary in prod for 5% of traffic with telemetry and automated rollback enabled.
Step 4: Gradually increase to 100% after 72h of stable metrics and run post-deployment drills.
rollback_plan: If error_rate > 1% absolute or p95_latency increases > 50% relative during a step, controller will automatically rollback to previous distribution and mark the target region as 'degraded' with a cooldown window of 10 minutes. Operators can trigger global rollback via console emergency action 'failover.abort'.
open_questions: Should 'serve_capacity' include predicted short-term allocation from ongoing autoscale events or only current headroom?
Do we need per-customer affinity rules during progressive shift to keep session consistency for chat-like flows?
What is the acceptable model_quality_score delta for low-risk customers vs enterprise customers?
next_actions: Diego to land probe smoothing PR and expose 'serving_ready' metric to routing controller (target: 2025-03-07).
SRE to add Grafana panels for cache_warmth, serve_capacity, and eviction_count (target: 2025-03-10).
PM to finalize runbook wording for support and add SLAs to playbook (target: 2025-03-12).
